question: What is the primary focus of health economics in the healthcare sector?
explanation: Health economics studies the distribution and allocation of limited resources to meet healthcare needs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why must nurse leaders understand basic economic principles in clinical practice?

options.A: To justify staffing levels and resource distribution
options.B: To manage personal investments and hospital shares
options.D: To calculate daily patient medication charges

explanation: Economic awareness empowers nurses to advocate for proper staffing and supplies by linking care quality to financial realities. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h1)

question: What does costing nursing services primarily involve?

options.A: Determining the monthly salary of the director of nursing
options.B: Reducing the number of shifts worked by junior nurses
options.C: Charging patients extra fees for basic bed baths
options.D: Measuring and assigning monetary value to consumed resources

explanation: Costing is the systematic process of finding the monetary value of all inputs used to deliver care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: What was a major disadvantage of traditional hospital billing systems regarding nursing?

options.A: Nursing care was hidden inside general room charges
options.B: Nurses were forced to collect cash payments directly
options.C: Hospital accountants overcharged for basic injections
options.D: Patient insurance companies refused to pay for nursing

explanation: Lumping nursing into room fees made the financial value of nursing invisible to hospital administrators. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: An example of a direct cost in nursing care is:

options.A: Sterile gloves used during a specific wound dressing
options.B: Monthly salary of the hospital human resource manager
options.C: Detergent used by the central laundry department
options.D: Electricity bills for running the entire hospital ward

explanation: Direct costs are tied directly to an individual patient, such as supplies used during a specific procedure. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following describes an indirect cost in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Expenses required to run the facility that cannot be tied to one patient
options.B: Disposable syringes used exclusively for an emergency resuscitation
options.C: Wages paid strictly to the nurse working a night shift on a medical ward
options.D: The exact cost of antibiotics prescribed to a single patient in the ward

explanation: Indirect costs are overhead expenses shared across the entire facility rather than assigned to a single care recipient. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a characteristic of fixed costs in a hospital ward?

options.A: They increase immediately when a new patient is admitted
options.B: They remain constant regardless of the patient population
options.C: They fluctuate based on the current cost of medications
options.D: They are calculated daily based on nursing hours worked

explanation: Fixed costs do not change when patient volume rises or falls within a normal operating range. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which item represents a variable cost during a sudden surge of malaria admissions?

options.A: Disposable IV infusion sets used for hydration
options.B: Monthly salary paid to the chief medical director
options.C: Depreciation value of the main hospital building
options.D: Annual maintenance contract for the generator

explanation: Variable costs rise and fall directly with the number of patients receiving treatment. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which costing method tracks every single resource and minute of care used by an individual patient?
explanation: Micro-costing involves detailed tracking of all individual inputs and time spent on a single patient. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is a major drawback of using the micro-costing methodology in clinical settings?

options.A: It relies entirely on vague estimations of ward overhead
options.B: It completely ignores the actual salary of the bedside nurse
options.C: It fails to account for basic supplies like cotton balls
options.D: It requires intensive and time-consuming data collection

explanation: While precise, micro-costing is expensive and difficult to implement due to the massive volume of data required. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Patient Classification System in nursing?

options.A: To categorize patients based on acuity and care needs
options.B: To determine the religious denomination of hospital staff
options.C: To calculate the annual depreciation of hospital beds
options.D: To assign fixed parking spaces to senior consultants

explanation: Patient Classification Systems group patients according to how sick they are and how much nursing care they require. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why does a patient requiring total care cost more to nurse than an ambulatory patient?

options.A: They require specialized surgical equipment for basic feeding
options.B: They demand significantly more direct nursing hours and resources
options.C: They consume more electricity from general ward overhead
options.D: They pay higher hospital admission fees upon arrival

explanation: High-acuity patients require intensive hands-on nursing time, which increases the labor cost component of their care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: A major operational barrier to accurate costing in many Nigerian public hospitals is:

options.A: Excessive availability of high-speed electronic health record software
options.B: Immediate automation of every nursing intervention in the ward
options.C: Reliance on manual paper-based record-keeping systems
options.D: Complete elimination of all direct out-of-pocket patient payments

explanation: Manual records make tracking minute-by-minute resource utilization and nursing time extremely difficult. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: How does the historical perception of nursing as a charitable vocation affect service costing?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any form of hospital budgeting
options.B: It ensures that nurses receive higher salaries than medical doctors
options.C: It forces hospital management to automate all nursing workloads
options.D: It creates institutional resistance to assigning monetary values to care

explanation: Viewing nursing as a purely altruistic duty causes administrators to overlook the economic realities of labor costs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: What tool do nurse managers use most effectively during budget negotiations when armed with costing data?

options.A: Evidence of patient acuity trends and labor costs
options.B: Personal threats of industrial strike action by staff
options.C: Unverified estimates of general hospital electricity use
options.D: Written complaints from patients about hospital food

explanation: Data on patient acuity and resource consumption provides objective backing for budget and staffing requests. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is financial literacy essential for modern nurse managers in healthcare organizations?

options.A: To replace the hospital chief financial officer during audits
options.B: To collect cash fees directly from patients at the ward desk
options.C: To participate in strategic planning and protect staffing budgets
options.D: To manage the personal financial portfolios of hospital board members

explanation: Understanding financial metrics allows nurse managers to secure necessary resources and influence organizational decisions. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)
